title: Model-routing cascade with verification: realised energy vs analytic work savings
research_question: Does a verified small-model cascade reduce facility energy per successful task, and how does the realised energy saving compare with the analytic saving in computational work?
hypothesis: With a perfect verifier the cascade reduces energy per successful task if and only if (small cost + verifier cost) < E[p_small] = 0.672; the realised fractional energy saving is smaller than the fractional work saving because idle, static, conversion and cooling energy do not scale with work. A verifier with false accepts lowers task success.
null_hypothesis: Energy saving tracks work saving one-to-one, or the break-even point differs from analytic.
independent_variables: routing on/off and small-model cost ratio
controlled_variables: task arrivals and outcome random numbers per seed
baseline: routing off (large model only) under the same policy
configuration: All routing parameters are hypothetical (class F); see registry
evaluation_criteria: Paired relative difference of each routing variant vs routing_off within policy; compare with analytic work ratio from workload.routing_expectations().
known_limitations: Quality model is a Bernoulli placeholder, not a measured model evaluation; verifier cost and accuracy are assumed; no batching effects.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
